clue.text: Century old prophecy which helped Britons across the water

definitions.text: which helped Britons across the water

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century
an oracle was the ancient source of prophecy, as at Delphi

explanation.surface: An ancient prediction from a hundred years ago that once aided the Britons.
explanation.walkthrough: A coracle is a small round boat of wicker and hide used by ancient Britons and still seen on Welsh rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: This light round boat carried early Britons over rivers, the description standing in for the vessel.

clue.text: The government case

explanation.surface: Simply the state's legal argument.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers form the executive body ruling Britain; a display cupboard is also called by this name.

clue.text: They help to make pretty face in periodical columns

definitions.text: They help to make pretty face

explanation.surface: A beauty article in a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Even, well-proportioned facial traits make someone handsome; recurring items in a newspaper or magazine are its standing columns.

clue.text: Sound sight for instance

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word pronounced like the next word

parts.note: the word heard, meaning a view

explanation.surface: A view that can be heard, as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: To quote something as an example is to give it for instance.

clue.text: Jewel of isle!

parts.note: Ireland is nicknamed after a green gemstone, so the jewel belongs to that island's name

explanation.surface: A precious stone belonging to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: This green gem gives Ireland its poetic nickname as a green isle.

clue.text: So lawful a way to seek custom

parts.note: licit means permitted by law

explanation.surface: A legal way of drumming up business.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking people for their trade or business is a way of soliciting orders.

clue.text: Bribed squad to go roundabout

indicators.note: the squad must surround the next piece, going round it

parts.note: taken as written
re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: Paying off a team of officers so they go round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: To square someone is slang for paying them off, corrupting with money.

clue.text: Let's change just in case

indicators.note: the letters of the word are told to change their order

explanation.surface: A suggestion to switch things around as a precaution.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means for fear that, introducing a precaution.

clue.text: Party lights on show in Beijing?

explanation.surface: Festive illumination seen in the capital of China.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper lamps hung at garden parties carry a Far Eastern name, so they would naturally appear in that capital.

clue.text: Muscular bands with enough fellows to form two quintets

parts.note: two groups of five make ten
dons are fellows of a university college

explanation.surface: Muscle bands with enough academics for two groups of five players.
explanation.definitionFit: These cords of tough tissue join muscle to bone.

clue.text: Asks the quiz-master for anether, but misses the point

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant wanting one more round but failing to grasp the issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally one pleads for a further quiz item; idiomatically the phrase means to evade the real issue by assuming the conclusion.

clue.text: Cromwell's head

explanation.surface: The leader of the Roundheads' top.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Cromwell was nicknamed 'Old' plus this short form of Oliver; it is also an old word for the crown of the skull.

clue.text: Esau was dangerous

explanation.surface: A biblical character was risky.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau was a shaggy man covered in body hair; informally the word also means risky or frightening.

clue.text: Planned mode of protest

indicators.note: planned suggests the letters are arranged afresh by design

explanation.surface: An organised way of registering dissent.
explanation.definitionFit: A street march or rally is a short form of demonstration.

clue.text: Measured up and prepared for paper hanging

explanation.surface: A wall checked and readied for wallpaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Graded by dimensions; also coated with glue-like size before decorating.

clue.text: Modify a repair

parts.note: to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: Altering a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: To change or correct a text is to revise it.

clue.text: Attempted to engulf Arkansas but lingered

indicators.note: engulf means to swallow up, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: tried means attempted
AR is the US postal abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: An army tried to swallow up a US state but dawdled.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay longer than needed or delay is to loiter.

clue.text: Piano felts chewed up down under

explanation.surface: Piano parts being eaten in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australia a damper is a simple bush bread baked in ashes, hence eaten 'down under'.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt pads stop a piano string vibrating; Australian bush bread is also called this, so is chewed there.

clue.text: Excuse the foreword?

explanation.surface: Justifying the preface of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A false reason is a cover story; read as pre-text it is what comes before the main words, a preface.

clue.text: Highly trained soldier gets 100 centavos for giving daytime protection

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, an elite soldier
the sol was a Peruvian currency unit of a hundred centavos

explanation.surface: An elite soldier gets paid in South American money for guarding by day.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is carried to protect against the sun in daylight.

clue.text: Tied up by trust it could be said

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the word heard, meaning faith

explanation.surface: Being bound by a trust, as might be stated.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird or prisoner bound tightly with string has been tied securely.

clue.text: Able to bid farewell to religious music

parts.note: can means is able to
ta-ta is an informal goodbye

explanation.surface: Capable of saying goodbye to church music.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral work, often on a sacred text, as Bach wrote for church services.

clue.text: Teased and separated the straw into short lengths

definitions.text: separated the straw into short lengths

explanation.surface: Mocked while cutting up straw.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantered with someone; also cut hay or straw into small pieces as animal fodder.

clue.text: Many set free

indicators.note: free means loose, so the letters are released into a new order

explanation.surface: A general release of many prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A general pardon releases a large number of prisoners at once.

clue.text: Strike breakers that plagued Hamelin

explanation.surface: Scabs who once troubled a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Pied Piper legend the town of Hamelin was overrun by vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who cross a picket line are insultingly called rodents; the rodents also infested Hamelin in the legend.

clue.text: French novelist of the French graduates

parts.note: du is French for of the
MAs are holders of a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A writer from France among French graduates.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas wrote The Three Musketeers.

clue.text: It teaches only ten letters of the alphabet

definitions.text: It teaches only ten letters of the alphabet

parts.words: It teaches only ten letters of the alphabet
parts.note: the school is spelt with four letters, those of 'ten' plus one more, so it seems to teach a tiny alphabet

explanation.surface: A school with a very limited alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous English public school's name is an anagram of 'ten' plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: This school near Windsor is a teaching institution, hence 'it teaches'.

clue.text: Ruin a cosmopolitan party

parts.note: un is French for a, the foreign word signalled by cosmopolitan
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Wrecking an international gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring to nothing or destroy is to wreck.

clue.text: Plant producing iron for British fleet

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A works making metal for the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A green flowerless plant with feathery fronds, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Expensive adornments emanating from long lines of subdued aristocracy

parts.note: strings are long lines
p, piano, means soft or subdued in music
earls are members of the aristocracy

explanation.surface: Costly jewellery coming from a quiet line of nobles.
explanation.definitionFit: Necklaces of gems from oysters are costly ornaments.

clue.text: Miss a definitive book brought down by the cowboy

parts.note: a miss is a young girl, a lass
the OED, Oxford English Dictionary, is the definitive reference

explanation.surface: A girl and a dictionary toppled by a cowboy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy catches and fells cattle with a looped rope.

clue.text: Royal family soap opera

explanation.surface: A royal household as a TV drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling house; also the title of an American 1980s television serial.
